questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 1 L closed flask contains a mixture of 4 g of methane and 4.4 g of carbon dioxide. The pressure inside the flask at $27^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ is [Assume ideal behaviour of gases]
questions.solution:
no. of moles of $\mathrm{CH}_4\left(\mathrm{n}_1\right)=\frac{4}{16}=0.25 \mathrm{~mol}$
no. of moles of $\mathrm{CO}_2\left(\mathrm{n}_2\right)=\frac{4.4}{44}=0.1 \mathrm{~mol}$
Total no. of moles $\left(\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{T}}\right)=\mathrm{n}_1+\mathrm{n}_2=0.35 \mathrm{~mol}\therefore \quad P=\frac{0.35 \times 0.082 \times 300}{1}=8.6 \mathrm{~atm}$

questions.q: In which mode of expression, the concentration of a solution remains independent of temperature?

Molality-Moles of solute/mass of solvent in kg

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An ideal gaseous mixture of ethane $\left(\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{6}\right)$ and ethene $\left(\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{4}\right)$ occupies 28 litre at 1 atm and $273 \mathrm{~K}$. The mixture reacts completely with $128 \mathrm{~g}\mathrm{O}_{2}$ to produce $\mathrm{CO}_{2} and \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O} .$ Mole fraction at $\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{6}$ in the mixture is:
questions.solution: $\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{6}+3.5 \mathrm{O}_{2} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{CO}_{2}+3 \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O} ;\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{4}+3 \mathrm{O}_{2} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{CO}_{2}+2 \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}$ Let volume of ethane is $\mathrm{x}$ litre, $22.4 \times 4=3.5 \mathrm{x}+3(28-\mathrm{x})\Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=11.2$ litre at constant $\mathrm{T}$ and $\mathrm{P}, \mathrm{V} \propto \mathrm{n} ;\Rightarrow$ Mole fraction of $\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{6}$ in mixture $=\frac{11.2}{28}=0.4$

questions.q: The amount of $\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{2}$ present in 1 litre of $1.5 \mathrm{ N} \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{2}$ solution, is:
questions.solution: Molecular weight of $\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{2}=34$ Equivalent weight of $\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{2}=17\therefore 1 \mathrm{ L}$ of $1 \mathrm{ N} \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{2} \mathrm{has}=17 \mathrm{ g}$ of $\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}\therefore 1$ Lof $1.5 \mathrm{NH}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{2}$ has $=1.5 \times 17=25.5 \mathrm{ g} \mathrm{of} \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{2}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In a compound $C, H$ and $N$ are present in $9: 1: 3. 5$ by weight. If molecular weight of compound is $108$, the molecular formula of compound is
questions.solution:
Element Ratio (by weight) Atomic weight Mol
Ratio		 Simplest Mol Ratio
$C$ $9$ $12$ $\dfrac{9}{12} = 0 . 75$ $\dfrac{0 . 75}{0 . 25} = 3$
$H$ $1$ $1$ $\dfrac{1}{1} = 1 . 00$ $\dfrac{1 . 00}{0 . 25} = 4$
$N$ $3 . 5$ $14$ $\dfrac{3 . 5}{14} = 0 . 25$ $\dfrac{0 . 25}{0 . 25} = 1$

$∴$ Empirical formula $= {C}_{3}{H}_{4}N$

The empirical formula mass $= 3 \times 12 + 4 \times 1 + 14 = 54g$

Given, molecular mass $= 108g$

Thus, $n = \dfrac{108}{54} = 2$

Hence, molecular formula = (Empirical formula) $\times 2$

$\left({C}_{3}{H}_{4}N\right) \times 2 = {C}_{6}{H}_{8}{N}_{2}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The empirical formula and molecular mass of a compound are ${CH}_{2}O$ and $180g$ respectively. The molecular formula of the compound will be
questions.solution:
As we know that,& the Molar mass of Carbon=12

Molar mass of Hydrogen=1

Molar mass of Oxygen=16

Empirical formula mass $= {CH}_{2}O = 12 + 2 + 1 \times 16 = 30$

Molecular mass $= 180$

$n = \dfrac{ Molccular Mass }{ Empirical formula mass } = \dfrac{100}{30} = 6$

$∵$ Molecular formula $= n \times$ empirical formula

$∴$ Molecular formula $= 6 \times {CH}_{2}O = {C}_{6}{H}_{12}{O}_{6}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: On electrolysis of water, a total of $1mole$ of gases is evolved. The amount of water decomposed is
questions.solution:
$∵$ Only one mole of total gases are evolved and ${H}_{2}O$ decomposes as

${H}_{2}O\overset{decomposition}{→}{H}_{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}{O}_{2}$

i.e. total moles $= 1 + \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{3}{2}$ moles by one mole of ${H}_{2}O$

Now,

$∵ \dfrac{3}{2}$ moles of gases are evolved by $= 1mole$ of ${H}_{2}O$

$∴ 1mole$ of gases are evolved by $= \dfrac{1}{3 / 2} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

Hence, $1mole$ of total gases are evolved by $\dfrac{2}{3}mole$ of ${H}_{2}O$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $0. 765g$ of an acid gives $0. 535g$ of ${CO}_{2}$ and $0. 138g$ of ${H}_{2}O$. Then, the ratio of percentage of carbon and hydrogen is&
questions.solution:
$%$ for ${CO}_{2}$

$∵ 0. 765g$ of acid gives ${CO}_{2} = 0. 535g$

$∴ 100g$ of acid gives ${CO}_{2} = \dfrac{0. 535 \times 100}{0. 765}$

$%$ of ${CO}_{2} = 70. 00$

$%$ for carbon

$∵ 44g$ of ${CO}_{2}$ gives, $C = 12g$

$∴ 70g$ of ${CO}_{2}$ gives, $C = \dfrac{12 \times 70}{44}$

$= 19. 09g$

$∴ %$ of carbon $= 19. 00$

Similarly,

(i) for hydrogen&

$%$ of ${H}_{2}O$

$⇒ \dfrac{0. 138 \times 100}{0. 765}$

$= 18. 03 = 18. 00$

$%$ of Hydrogen

$⇒ \dfrac{2 \times 18}{18} = 2. 00$

Hence ratio of carbon and hydrogen is $19: 2$

questions.q: $1.25 \mathrm{ g}$ of a sample of $\mathrm{Na}_{2} \mathrm{CO}_{3}$ and $\mathrm{Na}_{2} \mathrm{SO}_{4}$ is dissolved in $250 \mathrm{ml}$ solution. $25 \mathrm{ml}$ of this solution neutralises $20 \mathrm{ml}$ of $0.1 \mathrm{ N} \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{SO}_{4}$. The $\%$ of $\mathrm{Na}_{2} \mathrm{CO}_{3}$ in this sample is

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Formation of polyethylene from calcium carbide takes place as follows $\begin{array}{l}\mathrm{CaC}_{2}+2 \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Ca}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}+\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{2}$\\ $\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{2}+\mathrm{H}_{2} \longrightarrow \mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{4}$\\ $\mathrm{nC}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{4} \longrightarrow\left(-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\right)_{\mathrm{n}} \end{array}$ The amount of polyethylene obtained from $64.1 \mathrm{ kg}$ of $\mathrm{CaC}_{2}$ is
questions.solution: The concerned chemical reactions are (i) $\underset{64 \mathrm{ kg}}{\mathrm{CaC}_{2}+2 \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O} \rightarrow \mathrm{Ca}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}}+\underset{\text{ Ethyne, } 26 \mathrm{ kg}}{\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{2}}$ (ii) $\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{2}+\mathrm{H}_{2} \rightarrow \underset{\text{ Ethylene }, 28 \mathrm{ kg}}{\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{4}}\text{ (iii) } \mathrm{nC}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{2} \rightarrow\left[-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\right]_{\mathrm{n}}$\begin{array}{ll}$\mathrm{n}$ \times 28 $\mathrm{ kg}$ & $\mathrm{n}$ \times 28 $\mathrm{ kg} \text{ polythene }$ \\ $\text{$ or } 28 $\mathrm{ kg}$ & $\text{$ or } 28 $\mathrm{ kg}$\end{array}$ Thus $64 $\mathrm{ kg}$ of $\mathrm{CaC}_{2} gives$26 $\mathrm{ kg}$ of acetylene which in turn gives $28 \mathrm{ kg} of ethylene whose $28 $\mathrm{ kg}$ gives $28 \mathrm{ kg} of the polymer, polythene.$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Equal weights of $\mathrm{NaCl}$ and $\mathrm{KCl}$ are dissolved separately in equal volumes of solutions. Molarity of the two solutions will be :
options: That of $\mathrm{NaCl}$ will be less than that of $\mathrm{KCl}$
That of $\mathrm{NaCl}$ will be more than that of $\mathrm{KCl}$ solution
That of $\mathrm{NaCl}$ will be about half of that of $\mathrm{KCl}$ solution
questions.solution: When equal weights of different solutes are present in equal volumes of solution the molarity is inversely related to molecular mass of the solute. Mol. mass of $\mathrm{NaCl}$ is less than $\mathrm{KCl}$. Hence, molarity of $\mathrm{NaCl}$ solution will be more.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The product of atomic weight and specific heat of any element is a constant, approximately $6.4.$ This is known as:
questions.solution:
According to Dulong and Pettit's law
Atomic weight \times Specific heat $=6.4$ (approx) This law is applicable only to solid elements but it fails to explain very high specific heat of diamond.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The vapour density of ozone is
questions.solution:
We know that, Molecular weight of compound or molecules $=2 \times \mathrm{V}$. $\mathrm{D}$
Vapour density (V. D.) of ozone molecules
$=\frac{\mathrm{M}. \text{ wt. of } \mathrm{O}_{3}}{2}=\frac{48}{2}=24$
Hence, $\mathrm{V}. \mathrm{D}$. of $\mathrm{O}_{3}$ is 24
